claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand his current situation.

**Is Alex currently in full-time approved education or training?** For example, is he studying at school, college, or on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! Alex is still studying - he's doing his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and in full-time education, I need a bit more detail about his age.

**When did Alex turn 18, or when will he turn 19?** (I need to know his specific date of birth or at least which month he turned/will turn 18 or 19)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, he turned 18 earlier this year. He's still 18 now - won't be 19 until next year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question to complete my assessment:

**Are you the person responsible for Alex?** In other words, are you the one who looks after him and he lives with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives here at home with me and I look after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why: You can continue to claim Child Benefit for young people aged 16-19 who are in approved full-time education or training. Since Alex is 18 years old and studying A-levels at sixth form college (which counts as approved education), and he lives at home with you where you're responsible for him, you meet all the requirements.

**Important to note:** Child Benefit for young people in education generally continues until they turn 20, or until they leave full-time approved education or training - whichever comes first. This typically means you can claim until the end of the academic year in which they turn 19, or when they finish their course.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you're already receiving it, it should continue as long as Alex remains in full-time approved education.

Since Alex is still 18 (not yet 19) and is enrolled in full-time education at sixth form college, he meets the criteria. The claimant is responsible for Alex as he lives at home with them, which satisfies the requirement that the claimant must be responsible for the child. Therefore, the claimant is eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.
